Personally, at that price point I wouldn't buy if they didnt have a Goodyear welt. I think they require more maintenance than I am willing to give them and for a guy that needs a versatile boot that's used for hiking, working on the cars, doing endless house maintenance, fishing and all the rest well these just don't work for me. If you need cute little gimmicky booties for starbucks, shopping with your little expensive pain in the ass girlfriend at the debt inducing outlet stores, dinner at the Olive Garden and if you have the time for a sunset at the beach then by all means spend over $200 on these glorified bungalow clogs. I personally use the hundred dollar rule. Everything I have costs no more than $100 that I use on the regular, aside from the vehicles of course. I get old casios that work for decades, Wolverine boots that last for 3 years, house maintenance I do myself and along with most work on my 20 and 30 yr old Toyotas. I spend good money on 4 or 5 suits, decent tires, a good roof, good tools, 3 good generators, and things that make memories like 4 or 5 day vacations, those things are worth it. You want things to be like an old framing hammer from the 50s -- you just pick it up and it works.
